is a class that manages the various modes and types of selections within a grid.
It supports basic modes like single cell, row, column, and range selections, as well as advanced mode like negative ranges.
Events related to selections, such as changes to a selection, are propagated to listeners through the EventSelectionChangedListener interface.

content.text:
The AreaModelIf interface represents a model for a specific area of a table (header, body, or footer). It provides methods for accessing and manipulating data within that area. In the GuiExpert Table library, a table is divided into three main areas: - Header: Contains column titles and optional filter/sort controls - Body: Contains the main data of the table - Footer: Contains summary information or additional controls Each of these areas can be further divided into three sections: - West: Fixed columns on the left side - Center: Scrollable columns in the middle - East: Fixed columns on the right side 
 +----------------+-------------------+--------------+
 |  header/west   |  header/center    | header/east  |
 +----------------+-------------------+--------------+
 |  body/west     |  body/center      | body/east    |
 +----------------+-------------------+--------------+
 |  footer/west   |  footer/center    | footer/east  |
 +----------------+-------------------+--------------+
The AreaModelIf interface is a core component of the table's architecture. While simple tables might use basic data structures like arrays of arrays or arrays of objects, the GuiExpert Table library uses a more sophisticated model approach. An AreaModelIf implementation provides information about: - The number of rows in the area - The content of each cell - The styling of cells (CSS classes, custom styles) - Cell spanning (colspan, rowspan) - Row heights - Cell editability and selectability - Row selection state - Filtering and sorting capabilities This model-based approach provides maximum flexibility for creating complex, interactive tables.

readme.text:
is the framework-free core of the GuiExpert Table: virtual scrolling in both directions,
millions of rows, zero runtime dependencies, MIT-licensed. The framework packages (Angular, React, Vue,
Svelte, Solid, Preact, Web Component) are thin wrappers around exactly this API.

**New here?** The [training](https://gui.expert/training/) explains everything step by step – 36 short
chapters with live demos. Every chapter links back to the classes on this site.

## Where to start

| You want to … | Look at | Training |
|---|---|---|
| create and control a table | [TableScope](classes/TableScope.html), [TableApi](classes/TableApi.html) | [First table](https://gui.expert/training/first-table/) |

| configure behaviour and look | [TableOptions](classes/TableOptions.html), [TableOptionsIf](interfaces/TableOptionsIf.html) | [TableOptions](https://gui.expert/training/table-options/) |
| sort and filter | [TableApi.sortByColumn](classes/TableApi.html#sortByColumn), [TableOptionsIf.externalFilterFunction](interfaces/TableOptionsIf.html#externalFilterFunction) | [Sorting](https://gui.expert/training/sorting/), [Filtering](https://gui.expert/training/filtering/) |
